The mutation testing tool misclassified a hyphen in 'cuBLAS-like' (a compound word in a comment) as a 'cuda_Sub' operation. Python comments are completely ignored during parsing and execution - they contribute nothing to the program's semantics. The actual CUDA kernel code defined in the multi-line string starting at line 6 is byte-for-byte identical between the original and mutant. Since the compiled CUDA code is identical, the outputs will always be bitwise identical regardless of any input values. This explains why all 112 rounds of bitwise comparison and 138 rounds of enhanced testing showed perfect equivalence.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable. The mutation is in a Python comment, which has no effect on program execution. No input value, regardless of magnitude, distribution, or pattern, can cause any observable difference in output because the executable code paths are identical. The mutation testing tool made a classification error by treating a hyphen in natural language text as an arithmetic operator.
rounds.recommendations: Mutation testing tools should implement comment-awareness to avoid generating mutants from text inside comments or docstrings. A pre-filter that strips comments before identifying mutation sites would eliminate these false-positive unkillable mutants. Additionally, when a mutation tool reports a change with node_type 'cuda_Sub', verify that the context is actually executable code rather than a string literal or comment containing English text with hyphens.
